Author: Homer
Greek_Context: ἡ δ᾽ Οὔλυμπόνδε βεβήκει δώματ᾽ ἐς αἰγιόχοιο Διὸς μετὰ δαίμονας ἄλλους.
Philosophical_Note_on_Self_and_Interiori: Daimon denotes the Olympian gods as an external spatial collective; no link to human inwardness.

Author: Homer
Greek_Context: ἄλλα δὲ καὶ δαίμων ὑποθήσεται· οὐ γὰρ ὀΐω οὔ σε θεῶν ἀέκητι γενέσθαι τε τραφέμεν τε.
Philosophical_Note_on_Self_and_Interiori: The daimon acts from outside upon the hero's mind, prompting speech where human deliberation ends.

Author: Heraclitus
Philosophical_Note_on_Self_and_Interiori: Radical internalization: human character (ethos) replaces external divine agency as the locus of fate and selfhood.

Author: Plato
Greek_Context: ὅτι μοι θεῖόν τι καὶ δαιμόνιον γίγνεται... φωνή τις γιγνομένη, ἣ ὅταν γένηται, ἀεὶ ἀποτρέπει με τοῦτο ὃ ἂν μέλλω πράττειν.
Philosophical_Note_on_Self_and_Interiori: Experienced internally as a voice (phone), yet strictly inhibitory, preserving the autonomy of the rational self (autos).

Author: Plato
Greek_Context: τὸ δὲ δὴ περὶ τοῦ κυριωτάτου παρ᾽ ἡμῖν ψυχῆς εἴδους διανοεῖσθαι δεῖ τῇδε, ὡς ἄρα αὐτὸ δαίμονα θεὸς ἑκάστῳ δέδωκεν.
Philosophical_Note_on_Self_and_Interiori: Full philosophical synthesis: the highest, rational part of the soul (nous) is explicitly identified as the individual's inner daimon.
